paper.title: SteP: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions
paper.central_claim: SteP defines an MDP whose state is a stack of LLM policies, letting any policy act, invoke another policy or return control; dynamically composing a library of policies solves diverse web tasks, improving WebArena from 14.9% to 33.5% over SOTA GPT-4 single policies, staying competitive on MiniWoB++ with far less data, and using 2.3x fewer tokens than a flat prompt.
paper.scope_as_measured: WebArena 804 tasks (gpt-4-turbo-preview, 14 hand-written policies, single run); MiniWoB++ 45 non-visual tasks × 50 seeds (text-davinci-003); self-built AirlineCRM; three live airline sites compared with a human demonstration.

gap.author_gap: Single prompts covering all behaviours are long and leak; static hierarchies cannot adapt depth.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete: Flat-8k barely improves on Flat-4k and regresses some intents. Static-hierarchy residue argued (Fig. 1 recursion) but not tested.
gap.residue: Whether dynamic recursion (vs decomposition into short prompts) matters; generalisation beyond authored coverage.

assessment.author_claim_preserved: dynamic composition improves WebArena 14.9%→33.5% and MiniWoB++ with less data while using 2.3x fewer tokens
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With 14 hand-written, WebArena-intent-informed policies, a stack controller on gpt-4-turbo-preview reaches 0.33 macro success on all 804 WebArena tasks vs 0.20–0.23 for same-model flat prompts carrying the same material, using fewer input tokens per successful trajectory. Dynamic recursion vs decomposition, held-out generalisation and total cost are not established.
unresolved: 24 observation-action examples vs 21-example maximum not reconciled (O12, O11)

G.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Specific long-prompt/behaviour-leak bottleneck diagnosed by Flat-4k→8k; static-hierarchy residue argued only.

M.reason: Decided for sol. The stack MDP precisely changes information visibility (local histories) and control (push/act/pop, O10, O19); it yields distinguishable predictions against the naive alternatives — flat prompts degrade with length (tested via Flat-4k/8k) and static hierarchies fail on self-recursive tasks (Fig. 1, stated) — and its key assumption and failure boundary are explicit (O14). son55’s deductions ("recursion benefit not checked", "callee choice not tested") concern verification, which SCORE_SPEC assigns to E, not M.

X.reason: Both 3; confirmed with PDF Algorithm 1. Orchestration reconstructable; examples elided/external (O18), step budget unstated, wrong-call rate unmeasured.

E.measurement.reason: Both 3; confirmed. WebArena functional checkers on all 804 tasks (O01), MiniWoB rewards; CRM gold-action API and live-site human-demo comparison (O09) weaker.

E.causality.reason: Both 2; confirmed. Same-model Flat controls with the same material (O03), zero/few-shot; flat capped at 4k/8k (O17), unequal example capacity on MiniWoB (O11), no static/non-recursive control, prior works on other GPT-4 versions.

E.holdout.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Library built by clustering the evaluated WebArena intents (O02); MiniWoB demos from evaluated tasks; live sites judged against human demonstration (O09).

E.statistics.reason: Both 2; confirmed. Large denominators (804; 45×50 seeds; 20 scenarios) and per-intent tables; WebArena single run, no spread; n=3 sampling is not replication (O07).

E.cost.reason: Revised (neither seat’s value). Measured: input-token distribution vs Flat-8k and mean actions — real cost evidence (so not 1). But tokens are reported only over successful trajectories (O04) while the paper claims lower total cost and inference time (O05) without measuring calls, time or $; extra model calls are acknowledged (O06) and each call samples n=3 (O07); SteP takes more actions. Anchor 2 ("相关结果，关键控制、覆盖缺口尚存"). Calibrated against this batch: LASER (cap only, 1) < SteP < AutoDroid (tokens+$+latency on all prompts, same backbone, 3).
